lessons.title: Diagnostic and tensor shapes
lessons.goal: Explain a neuron, Bayes rule, a matrix product and your thesis aloud; score each 0–3.
lessons.code: Create tensors; distinguish reshape, transpose and broadcasting.

lessons.title: Linear algebra for representations
lessons.goal: Compute dot products and projections; explain rank, eigenvectors and SVD geometrically.
lessons.code: Check matrix multiplication shapes and compare a low-rank reconstruction.

lessons.title: Calculus and computation graphs
lessons.goal: Derive a scalar chain rule, a gradient and the gradient of a squared-error linear predictor.
lessons.code: Compare an analytic gradient with autograd and finite differences.

lessons.title: Probability and statistical evidence
lessons.goal: Work through conditional probability, expectation, likelihood and sampling uncertainty.
lessons.code: Simulate class imbalance; calculate precision, recall and a bootstrap interval.

lessons.title: Asymptotic analysis and recurrences
lessons.goal: Derive merge-sort complexity; distinguish worst-case, expected and amortized bounds.
lessons.code: Implement and count operations for two input sizes.

lessons.title: Sorting, searching and hashing
lessons.goal: Trace quicksort and binary search invariants; compare collision strategies.
lessons.code: Write binary search and test empty/boundary cases.

lessons.title: Linear and logistic regression
lessons.goal: Derive squared-error and logistic gradients; explain regularization and decision thresholds.
lessons.code: Fit a tiny regression model with an explicit training loop.

lessons.title: Generalization and evaluation
lessons.goal: Distinguish bias/variance, leakage, class imbalance and calibration; construct a safe split.
lessons.code: Implement a confusion matrix and test threshold changes.

lessons.title: SVM and tree ensembles
lessons.goal: Explain maximum margin, slack and kernel intuition; contrast bagging with boosting.
lessons.code: Plot a toy boundary; explain why scaling affects distance-based methods.

lessons.title: PCA, clustering and naive Bayes
lessons.goal: Work a PCA projection and one k-means update; explain EM responsibilities and independence assumptions.
lessons.code: Compare projected data with the original covariance matrix.

lessons.title: Lists, stacks, queues and trees
lessons.goal: Trace pointer changes and traversals; explain BST invariants and heap operations.
lessons.code: Implement traversal and test a malformed edge case.

lessons.title: Heaps and amortized analysis
lessons.goal: Explain O(n) build-heap and amortized dynamic-array growth.
lessons.code: Compare repeated insertion with bottom-up heap construction.

lessons.title: MLP forward and backward passes
lessons.goal: Trace a two-layer network; derive one weight gradient and state every tensor dimension.
lessons.code: Build a tiny MLP; compare manual and automatic gradients.

lessons.title: Optimization and initialization
lessons.goal: Compare SGD, momentum and AdamW; explain learning-rate schedules and variance-preserving initialization.
lessons.code: Record gradient norms under two initialization scales.

lessons.title: Normalization and regularization
lessons.goal: Compute normalization axes; compare BatchNorm and LayerNorm at train and evaluation time.
lessons.code: Inspect running statistics and dropout behavior in train()/eval().

lessons.title: CNN mechanics and receptive fields
lessons.goal: Derive convolution output sizes, parameters and receptive fields; distinguish correlation and convolution.
lessons.code: Implement a tiny convolution using loops and compare with Conv2d.

lessons.title: BFS, DFS and topological order
lessons.goal: Trace queue/stack state; distinguish directed and undirected cycle detection.
lessons.code: Implement BFS distances and topological sorting.

lessons.title: Shortest paths and minimum spanning trees
lessons.goal: State Dijkstra assumptions; compare Bellman-Ford, Prim and Kruskal.
lessons.code: Construct a negative-edge counterexample to naive Dijkstra.

lessons.title: Word representations and tokenization
lessons.goal: Compare one-hot, TF-IDF, CBOW, skip-gram, negative sampling and subword representations.
lessons.code: Prepare CBOW context-target pairs and inspect Indic tokenizer outputs.

lessons.title: RNN, LSTM and GRU internals
lessons.goal: Trace recurrent state and gates; explain how gradient paths differ without claiming vanishing gradients disappear.
lessons.code: Trace a two-step recurrent cell and detach hidden state deliberately.

lessons.title: Sequence-to-sequence and attention
lessons.goal: Explain teacher forcing, encoder-decoder state transfer, alignment and exposure bias.
lessons.code: Implement a small attention-weighted context vector.

lessons.title: Transformer from input to logits
lessons.goal: Draw embeddings, attention, residuals, normalization and FFN; distinguish all masks.
lessons.code: Implement scaled dot-product attention with a causal mask.

lessons.title: Dynamic programming
lessons.goal: Derive state, recurrence, initialization and reconstruction for LCS/edit distance.
lessons.code: Implement edit distance with a table and recover an alignment.

lessons.title: Greedy proofs and complexity classes
lessons.goal: Explain exchange arguments, P/NP and reduction direction using a concrete example.
lessons.code: Contrast a greedy rule with an exhaustive solution on tiny inputs.

lessons.title: Language-model objectives
lessons.goal: Compare autoregressive, masked and denoising objectives using GPT, BERT and T5/mBART.
lessons.code: Build labels and ignored positions for a toy training batch.

lessons.title: Position and context
lessons.goal: Explain sinusoidal positions, RoPE and relative positions; distinguish sequence length from embedding width.
lessons.code: Apply a two-dimensional rotation and check dot-product behavior.

lessons.title: Decoding and sequence evaluation
lessons.goal: Trace greedy and beam decoding; distinguish temperature, top-k and top-p; compute CER/WER.
lessons.code: Implement edit-distance dynamic programming and a tiny beam search.

lessons.title: Transfer, multilinguality and correction
lessons.goal: Explain tokenization costs, fine-tuning, language tags and over-correction in your own systems.
lessons.code: Compare token counts and correction errors across two scripts.

lessons.title: Relational model and algebra
lessons.goal: Map ER entities and keys; trace selection, projection, join and division.
lessons.code: Express a query in relational algebra and SQL.

lessons.title: SQL and joins
lessons.goal: Explain nulls, grouping, outer joins and correlated subqueries.
lessons.code: Run queries on a tiny database with missing values.

lessons.title: Image processing and local features
lessons.goal: Trace filtering, edges and morphology; explain SIFT stages and the source of invariances.
lessons.code: Apply filters to a toy image and inspect boundary handling.

lessons.title: Geometry and estimation
lessons.goal: Compare translation, rigid, similarity, affine and projective transforms; state degrees of freedom and RANSAC assumptions.
lessons.code: Transform points in homogeneous coordinates and check preserved properties.

lessons.title: ResNet, detection and segmentation
lessons.goal: Trace residual stages and pooling; compare two-stage detection, YOLO, U-Net and instance segmentation.
lessons.code: Record shapes at each ResNet stage for two input resolutions.

lessons.title: ViT and self-supervised vision
lessons.goal: Trace patch embedding and position; compare ViT, Swin, contrastive learning and masked reconstruction.
lessons.code: Extract patches and count tokens for multiple aspect ratios.

lessons.title: Functional dependencies and normal forms
lessons.goal: Compute closure; distinguish 3NF/BCNF, losslessness and dependency preservation.
lessons.code: Work a decomposition and show a spurious-tuple counterexample.

lessons.title: Indexes and query execution
lessons.goal: Explain B+ trees, selectivity and clustered indexes; trace a join strategy.
lessons.code: Inspect a simple query plan before and after an index.

lessons.title: Decoder internals and efficient attention
lessons.goal: Trace normalization, RoPE, FFN and residual paths; compare MHA/MQA/GQA and exact attention implementations.
lessons.code: Calculate attention and KV-cache sizes from an explicit config.

lessons.title: Adaptation and quantization
lessons.goal: Explain LoRA rank, QLoRA purpose and frozen versus trainable parameters; separate numerical precision from model size.
lessons.code: Implement a low-rank weight update and count trainable parameters.

lessons.title: Training and post-training
lessons.goal: Compare pretraining, SFT, preference learning and reasoning-oriented training; identify assumptions in reported evaluations.
lessons.code: Inspect prompt/response loss masks and make a leakage checklist.

lessons.title: Retrieval and reliable generation
lessons.goal: Trace retrieval, reranking and context construction; evaluate retrieval separately from generation.
lessons.code: Build a tiny local lexical retriever and inspect its failures.

lessons.title: Transactions and concurrency
lessons.goal: Trace conflict serializability, locking, isolation levels and deadlocks.
lessons.code: Draw a precedence graph for two schedules.

lessons.title: Recovery and DBMS consolidation
lessons.goal: Explain write-ahead logging and checkpoints; solve mixed normalization/transaction questions.
lessons.code: Trace a crash and identify undo/redo needs under stated assumptions.

lessons.title: CLIP and cross-modal alignment
lessons.goal: Explain contrastive targets, normalization and similarity; distinguish retrieval alignment from text generation.
lessons.code: Construct a small image-text similarity matrix and both loss directions.

lessons.title: Projectors, resamplers and fusion
lessons.goal: Compare a projected visual-token sequence, query-based resampling and cross-attention; inspect a selected checkpoint.
lessons.code: Trace visual width to language width and count connector parameters.

lessons.title: Variable resolution and spatial positions
lessons.goal: For a pinned model version, trace resize policy, patch grid, merging, positions, batching and visual-token count.
lessons.code: Log processor output shapes for three aspect ratios; distinguish padding stages.

lessons.title: Document and video inputs
lessons.goal: Compare page crops, layout, temporal sampling and token budgets; track information lost before generation.
lessons.code: Measure character height after resizing and record token budget per image.

lessons.title: Network layers and link protocols
lessons.goal: Trace encapsulation; explain framing, CRC and medium access.
lessons.code: Work one small XOR-based CRC example.

lessons.title: IP addressing and subnetting
lessons.goal: Calculate masks, network boundaries and host ranges; explain CIDR and routing prefixes.
lessons.code: Solve subnet examples and verify binary representations.

lessons.title: VAE and GAN mechanisms
lessons.goal: Explain latent variables, reconstruction/KL trade-offs and adversarial objectives; identify what is optimized.
lessons.code: Calculate a toy Gaussian KL term and inspect reconstruction error.

lessons.title: Diffusion fundamentals
lessons.goal: Trace forward corruption and reverse prediction; distinguish training loss from sampling procedure.
lessons.code: Corrupt a tiny tensor at several noise levels using a fixed seed.

lessons.title: Statistical and robustness evaluation
lessons.goal: Separate paired comparisons, confidence intervals, subgroup errors and distribution shift.
lessons.code: Bootstrap paired per-example differences; inspect domain-specific failures.

lessons.title: Controlled architecture experiment
lessons.goal: Choose one preprocessing or token-budget hypothesis; state its control, confound and falsification condition.
lessons.code: Run a small matched-budget comparison and save an experiment table.

lessons.title: Routing, ARP, DHCP and NAT
lessons.goal: Trace a packet between subnets; compare distance-vector and link-state routing.
lessons.code: Draw a packet path including address changes.

lessons.title: TCP, UDP and congestion
lessons.goal: Explain handshake, reliability, flow control and congestion control separately.
lessons.code: Trace sequence/acknowledgment numbers through a lost segment.

lessons.title: Explicit tool-use loop
lessons.goal: Distinguish a fixed workflow from model-directed control; trace messages, tools, state and stopping conditions.
lessons.code: Implement a deterministic mock model-tool-observation loop without paid APIs.

lessons.title: Tools, state and failure handling
lessons.goal: Define schemas, validation, timeouts, retries and permissions; distinguish memory from conversation history.
lessons.code: Inject a malformed tool result and test bounded recovery.

lessons.title: Frameworks after mechanisms
lessons.goal: Map one current framework to the loop you implemented; inspect its official docs and pin its version.
lessons.code: Recreate the same small workflow in one framework; compare traces.

lessons.title: Evaluate an agentic research idea
lessons.goal: Compare a fixed correction workflow with an adaptive one; measure correctness, cost and failure cascades.
lessons.code: Use saved/mock outputs first; log tool success and task success separately.

lessons.title: DNS, HTTP and TLS overview
lessons.goal: Explain what happens after entering a URL and where caching occurs.
lessons.code: Inspect a local HTTP request and response; identify headers.

lessons.title: Processes, threads and memory
lessons.goal: Explain scheduling, virtual memory, paging and deadlock conditions.
lessons.code: Trace a page-table lookup with a small address example.

lessons.title: Defend your first contribution
lessons.goal: Explain the problem, novelty, strongest baseline, ablations, limitations and your personal role.
lessons.code: Reproduce one reported metric from a small saved example.

lessons.title: Defend complementary views
lessons.goal: Explain when a second view adds information, when it conflicts and how to test dependence on translation quality.
lessons.code: Create controlled corruptions and compare single-view versus dual-view behavior.

lessons.title: Find and challenge a research gap
lessons.goal: Separate established facts, observations and hypotheses; search primary literature before claiming novelty.
lessons.code: Specify a minimal falsifying experiment with a matched-compute baseline.

lessons.title: Build a reproducibility record
lessons.goal: Document splits, normalization, seeds, model revisions, prompt templates and evaluation choices.
lessons.code: Write a small evaluation entry point and a configuration record.

lessons.title: Core-CS teaching demo
lessons.goal: Teach Dijkstra or normalization with an example, assumptions and a check question.
lessons.code: Prepare an executable example and its edge case.

lessons.title: Mixed core-CS problems
lessons.goal: Solve a timed mixture; explain wrong options and update your error log.
lessons.code: Reproduce two mistakes with minimal examples.

lessons.title: Teach backpropagation
lessons.goal: Deliver a 10-minute undergraduate explanation using one scalar example before matrix notation.
lessons.code: Create a tiny gradient demonstration with assertions.

lessons.title: Teach attention or convolution
lessons.goal: Deliver a second teaching demo; anticipate misconceptions and include one worked example.
lessons.code: Build a two-query attention or convolution visualization from small arrays.

lessons.title: Research talk and future programme
lessons.goal: Prepare short and full versions; state two feasible future projects and the first experiment for each.
lessons.code: Prepare one clean figure/table from your research pipeline.

lessons.title: Role-specific application package
lessons.goal: Refine CV, research and teaching statements; map your skills to one real advertisement.
lessons.code: Check that links, repository instructions and examples are reproducible.

lessons.title: DSA repair
lessons.goal: Revisit the weakest graph or DP topic; explain correctness before writing code.
lessons.code: Solve a new instance without a solution template.

lessons.title: DBMS repair
lessons.goal: Revisit the weakest normalization, SQL or concurrency topic.
lessons.code: Test your reasoning on an unfamiliar schema/schedule.

lessons.title: Technical mock and diagnostic repair
lessons.goal: Answer a mixed set aloud; score correctness, reasoning, clarity and recovery from uncertainty.
lessons.code: Reimplement the concept you could not explain.

lessons.title: Research defence mock
lessons.goal: Answer challenges about novelty, data validity, baselines, failure modes and practical value.
lessons.code: Verify the key numerical claim and a failure case.

lessons.title: Architecture reconstruction challenge
lessons.goal: Draw one selected model cold from raw input to prediction, then inspect code to locate errors.
lessons.code: Use hooks or intermediate outputs to verify the disputed shapes.

lessons.title: Targeted foundation repair
lessons.goal: Choose the lowest-confidence foundational concept from your error log; solve a new example.
lessons.code: Write a unit check that fails under your earlier misconception.

lessons.title: CN and OS repair
lessons.goal: Revisit the weakest packet-flow, subnetting or memory topic.
lessons.code: Work a numerical example and explain each intermediate result.

lessons.title: Written-test rehearsal
lessons.goal: Attempt a timed mixed core-CS set using free official past questions where available.
lessons.code: Classify each miss as concept, calculation or time-management.

lessons.title: Mixed recall without notes
lessons.goal: Explain connections across representations, optimization, attention and evaluation; revisit unresolved gaps.
lessons.code: Rebuild a short training loop without copying a tutorial.

lessons.title: Full interview rehearsal
lessons.goal: Combine introduction, teaching, technical questions and research vision; record timing and errors.
lessons.code: Prepare a runnable miniature demo relevant to your claimed expertise.

lessons.title: Research synthesis and next experiment
lessons.goal: Select one supported research question; define baseline, budget, outcome and stopping condition.
lessons.code: Create the smallest reproducible experiment scaffold.

lessons.title: January review and continuation
lessons.goal: Review evidence of mastery, remaining weaknesses and your realistic workload after joining a role.
lessons.code: Clean notebooks and create a monthly maintenance checklist.

lessons.title: Teach outside your speciality
lessons.goal: Explain an undergraduate core concept clearly and answer follow-up questions.
lessons.code: Build one five-line example that exposes a misconception.

lessons.title: Core-CS final retrieval
lessons.goal: Solve representative questions across DSA, DBMS, CN and essential OS.
lessons.code: Create a concise list of remaining fragile concepts.

lessons.title: Flexible repair and catch-up
lessons.goal: Use this slot for unfinished priority work; do not add a new model family.
lessons.code: Verify an unresolved implementation question.

lessons.title: Readiness review and next-month plan
lessons.goal: Review mastery evidence; choose next month’s weak concepts and research investigation.
lessons.code: Archive a runnable example and export a complete backup.

questions.q: Why does L2 regularization change the solution?
questions.guide: Explain the objective and gradient; connect penalty strength to model flexibility. Distinguish regularization from a guarantee of improved test performance.

questions.q: When is accuracy misleading?
questions.guide: Discuss class prevalence, error costs, precision/recall and thresholds. Give a numerical imbalanced-data example.

questions.q: What is a gradient, and why do tensor dimensions matter?
questions.guide: Explain a local direction of greatest increase, the chain rule and the shape of a derivative. Work one scalar-to-vector example.

questions.q: Derive one weight gradient in a two-layer network.
questions.guide: Write forward equations, identify the upstream derivative, apply the chain rule and verify dimensions.

questions.q: Why use residual connections?
questions.guide: Explain the identity path and additive gradient term. Discuss optimization without claiming all gradient problems disappear.

questions.q: How do BatchNorm and LayerNorm differ?
questions.guide: Specify normalized axes, learned affine terms, train/eval behavior and why batch statistics matter.

questions.q: How do CBOW and skip-gram differ?
questions.guide: Identify input/target direction, shared embedding tables and the training objective; explain negative sampling separately.

questions.q: What does the attention scaling factor do?
questions.guide: Discuss dot-product variance under assumptions, softmax saturation and the role of head dimension. Do a small calculation.

questions.q: Which mask is needed during training and generation?
questions.guide: Separate causal, padding and loss masks; trace visible positions and ignored targets.

questions.q: Compare BERT, GPT and T5 objectives.
questions.guide: Explain context visibility, targets and encoder/decoder roles; connect those choices to a task.

questions.q: Must ResNet receive a 224×224 image?
questions.guide: Distinguish a preprocessing recipe from architectural constraints. Inspect convolutional layers, pooling and classifier dimensions in the selected implementation.

questions.q: What makes SIFT approximately scale invariant?
questions.guide: Trace scale-space extrema, localization, orientation and descriptor construction; explain limits of the invariance.

questions.q: Trace an image through a selected VLM.
questions.guide: Name the exact checkpoint/config; trace resize/crop, patch grid, vision encoder, connector, position handling and language-model input.

questions.q: Are patch size, token width and token count the same?
questions.guide: Define each quantity; calculate one grid; explain where merging or resampling changes sequence length.

questions.q: Does avoiding image padding mean no padding anywhere?
questions.guide: Distinguish image processing, packed vision sequences, language batching and masks. Verify the specific code path.

questions.q: How do LoRA and KV caching solve different problems?
questions.guide: LoRA changes adaptation parameterization; KV caching reuses inference states. Explain costs and limitations separately.

questions.q: How is an agent different from a fixed workflow?
questions.guide: Discuss who controls the sequence of operations; trace state, tool calls, observations and stopping conditions.

questions.q: How would you evaluate an agent beyond answer accuracy?
questions.guide: Include task success, tool errors, cost, latency, retries and unsafe actions; compare with a fixed pipeline.

questions.q: Why does Dijkstra need nonnegative edge weights?
questions.guide: Explain the finalized-distance invariant and provide a counterexample with a negative edge.

questions.q: Derive edit distance and its complexity.
questions.guide: Define prefixes, substitution/deletion/insertion transitions, boundaries, O(mn) time and memory trade-offs.

questions.q: Does BCNF decomposition always preserve dependencies?
questions.guide: Distinguish lossless join from dependency preservation; work an explicit dependency set.

questions.q: How do you test conflict serializability?
questions.guide: Build a precedence graph from conflicting operations of different transactions; test for a cycle.

questions.q: Distinguish TCP flow control and congestion control.
questions.guide: Explain receiver capacity versus network load, advertised window and congestion window.

questions.q: Why correct recognition output instead of improving the recognizer?
questions.guide: State the deployment constraints and complementary value; acknowledge cases where recognizer improvement is the stronger baseline.

questions.q: How do you show that a second view adds useful information?
questions.guide: Compare matched single/dual-view baselines, corrupt or shuffle the second view, stratify disagreements and control compute.

questions.q: How could your evaluation overstate improvements?
questions.guide: Discuss leakage, synthetic-to-real gaps, tuning on test data, normalization, baseline strength and uncertainty.

questions.q: Teach attention to an undergraduate in ten minutes.
questions.guide: Start with a small weighted-retrieval example, add Q/K/V, calculate weights and finish with a diagnostic question.

questions.q: What would you do in your first three months in this role?
questions.guide: Give a scoped problem, accessible data, baseline, falsifiable experiment, resource budget and deliverable.
